title: Water: what each kind of cooling uses
alt: A section along a plant yard. City water comes from a main under the street through a meter and runs under the yard. Three cooling units stand side by side: an air-cooled chiller with no water pipe, a hybrid cooler whose pads are wet and dripping, and a cooling tower giving off vapour, with a pipe from its base to the sewer.
sources: kit3d SPEC chill: Vertiv Liebert AFC FIZ135 (SL-71060 R09/24, preliminary data)
kit3d SPEC hybrid: EVAPCO eco-Air EAW-VA, EA26MRKT (2026) p.13; p.8 wetted pads outside both coil faces
kit3d SPEC tower: BAC Series 3000 S3E-1222-07R (Engineering Data C15-C16, 2023)
tool Cooling and water card: air-cooled chillers use no water (physics); towers: evaporation and blowdown (FEMP); hybrid: wet hours above a set point
drawn_generically: water main, meter pit, sewer and pipe routes
heat arrows over the chiller and hybrid (a picture, not a plume study)

steps.caption: City water comes in from the main under the street, through a meter.
An air-cooled chiller uses no water: fans push the heat into the air.
A hybrid cooler wets its pads only on hot days.
A cooling tower evaporates water all year to carry the heat away.
Some water is flushed to the sewer so minerals don't build up.
No water, water on hot days, or water all year: it depends on the cooling.

camera: face-on section; slides from the street main along the three units, then pulls back over the yard
status: new (23qz d); no water quantities shown, because the tool's tower and hybrid figures are rated weak to moderate in the 23 Nov audit
